destination: Australia (3 weeks); the £1,000 is the deposit, due in 30 days

characters.dave: Dad, 41, fixes washing machines, furthest trip Skegness, moustache, blue overalls
characters.sue: Mum, 40, runs the house, the budget and the family group chat, curly red hair, glasses, pink cardigan
characters.ellie: 15, glued to her phone, purple hoodie, long dark hair; her best friend's birthday concert is next Saturday (£45 ticket)
characters.alfie: 8, dreams of seeing a real kangaroo, spiky blond hair, green koala t-shirt; plays the kangaroo in his school play (kangaroo-ear costume)
characters.crumbs: the dog, has eaten three TV remotes this year
characters.bev: the gardener from down the street, grey curls, orange bobble hat, green jumper, wellies; non-speaking so far
characters.launderette: the launderette on the high street: 10 broken machines; another repairman fixed 5, Dave fixed the other 5 after the play for £20 each (non-speaking)

episodes.summary: Intro. Sue finds 3 weeks in Australia; they need a £1,000 deposit in 30 days. Jar has £23.50.

options.A: Car boot sale (sell garage junk): +£, HOUSE up, Alfie may lose toys
options.B: Dave takes weekend repair jobs: +££, Dave tired, happiness down
options.C: Ellie sells her old clothes online: +£, Ellie NOT happy ('Not my clothes!')

episodes.summary: Vote A (1-0-0): car boot sale. Sold £78 of garage junk, -£10 pitch fee, -£3.50 because Crumbs ate a customer's bacon roll: +£64.50, fund £88.00. Alfie sold his dinosaurs ('I'm a kangaroo person now'), Ellie went undercover in sunglasses. Happiness 50->55, house 22->40 (garage empty). Cliffhanger: back home Crumbs buried the car keys in the garden; Dave needs the car for work tomorrow at 8am.

options.A: Dig up the whole garden: free, HOUSE down, might not find the keys
options.C: Dave rides to work on Alfie's tiny bike: free, Dave tired, happiness down

episodes.summary: Vote A (2-0-0): dug up the garden overnight. Sue split it into a string grid and logged squares in the group chat, Ellie's phone was the torch (9% battery), Alfie tried to dig to Australia. At 1am they found a sock, a tennis ball and Crumbs' 3 missing TV remotes (he buries them). 7:50am, 14 holes, no keys; then Crumbs sniffed one spot and dug them up in 10 seconds. Dave made it to work with 2 minutes to spare. Cost £0, fund stays £88.00. Happiness 55->50 (no sleep), house 40->25 (14 holes). New problem: the garden looks like the moon and the neighbours are staring; Alfie suggests crazy golf.

options.A: Fill every hole back in: free, HOUSE up, takes Dave's day off (happiness down)
options.B: Crazy golf for the street at £2 a round: +£, garden stays a mess, Ellie mortified ('I'm moving to the moon')
options.C: Pay a gardener: -£60, HOUSE way up

episodes.summary: No votes (0-0-0), so Crumbs chose: he sat on C, pay a gardener £60. 9am Bev the gardener arrived with a wheelbarrow and a very big spade. Dave: '£60? I could have done that myself!' Sue: 'You fell asleep in your cornflakes.' Two hours: 14 holes filled, grass seed down. Neighbours stopped staring (Ellie relieved), Alfie mourned his tunnel to Australia. -£60: fund £88.00 -> £28.00 (nearly back to day 1's £23.50). House 25->65, happiness 50->55. Twist: Bev spotted Dave's overalls; her washing machine has been broken for a month. Dave: 'That's my thing!'

options.A: Fix it for free as a thank you: £0, happiness up, Bev owes them one
options.C: Sue advertises Dave's repairs in the street group chat (94 people): £30 a job, uncertain how many, Dave's evenings gone

episodes.summary: Vote C (2-1-0): Sue posted Dave's repairs (£30 a job) in the street group chat (94 people). 5 bookings in 10 minutes; Sue made a colour-coded spreadsheet. Ellie: Dad got 37 mentions in the chat, she got 0 ('Literally embarrassing'). Dave worked door to door 6pm-11pm: Bev (No. 9) first, then Nos. 14, 22, 31 and 40. No. 40's machine was just unplugged ('That one wasn't broken. It was unplugged'), so no charge. 4 paid jobs x £30 = £120, minus £15 parts: +£105 (best night yet), fund £28.00 -> £133.00. Dave missed Alfie's bedtime story; Crumbs 'read' it and ate page 4. Happiness 55->45, house stays 65. Twist: the launderette on the high street offers £200 to fix 10 broken machines tomorrow at 2pm, the same time as Alfie's school play (he's the kangaroo). Dave: '£200? That's three trips to Skegness!'

options.A: Take the launderette job: +£200, Dave misses Alfie's school play (happiness down)
options.B: Go to the play: £0, happiness up, turn down the £200
options.C: Start at 6am and race back for 2pm: +£200 if he's quick, but one delay and he misses the play (risky)

episodes.vote_rule: no A/B/C votes: random (Crumbs chose). One viewer wrote in 'D go at 5 am' and 'Or go after play'; the second idea was used as a twist

episodes.summary: No A/B/C votes (0-0-0), so Crumbs chose again: he sat on B, go to the play. Dave turned down the £200 ('Sorry! Kangaroo duty.'). Alfie on stage: 'Hop, hop, hop! I'm the best kangaroo in Year Four!' Dave: 'I'm not crying. It's the washing powder.' Ellie filmed it: 'Mum, do not put it in the group chat.' Sue: 'Too late. 94 people have seen it.' Twist from a real viewer comment ('Or go after play'): Dave rang the launderette; another repairman had already fixed half, so Dave fixed the other 5 until 9pm at £20 each: +£100, fund £133.00 -> £233.00 (£767 to go). Happiness 45->60, house stays 65. New problem: Ellie's best friend's birthday concert next Saturday, tickets £45; Ellie: 'If I miss it, I literally don't exist.' Alfie: 'Ellie, with no phone for a week? She'll explode!'

options.A: Pay from the holiday jar: -£45, Ellie happy (happiness up)
options.C: Sponsored no-phone week: the street chat pays for the ticket, but only if Ellie lasts 7 days; fail = no concert
